report:
# PG-ADMISSION-FLOOR

Read PrimitiveAdmissionFloor.lean (sha df9d149bbd06, Core Lean, no Mathlib) and PointedRelation.lean (sha 2d36b5427b54): the cut theorems are general and correct (apartness, subsingleton refusal, identification) but the instance/law singleton theorems are stated only on Unit, and pointed_relation_independence is over Type u with the third clause needing irreflexivity. The local aggregate (DerivationDagQMClosure.lean line 1257) is a fixed enumeration. Re-proved all of them for arbitrary carriers and added: cut existence iff two distinct points, the exact converse of identification_breaks_law, and law-from-distinctness independence on every nontrivial carrier. The law is supplied: the node (as the DAG bottleneck says) does not derive it from <> or Real_0 and neither does this bundle.

Supported: Kernel-checked for arbitrary carriers: an exhibited cut has distinct endpoints, a cut exists on V iff V has two distinct points, no cut exists on a subsingleton, a map carrying the relation into an irreflexive target separates the endpoints and (sharper) such a target exists iff the map separates every related pair; instance-without-law and law-without-instance exist, and the three pointed-relation facts hold. Native: every relation on 0..4 points (65536 at n=4) tabulated by cut data, law, instance and the four related/equal quadrants, and every irreflexive relation, map and target on 1..3 points, all matching closed forms with zero exceptions.

Remaining: Deriving the law (irreflexivity) from the primitive difference <> or from Real_0: the relation and its law remain supplied data; any selection of a preferred cut or orientation (two orientations exist on two points); infinite carriers beyond the Lean statements; the arity-cost tie-breaker of the source (declared_arity_cost_selects is a decide on a priced toy, not used here); the aggregate local theorem pg_to_sn_and_wdp_route_chain_composition, which is a fixed enumeration.
construction: Bitmask enumeration of every relation on 0..4 points and every (irreflexive relation, map, irreflexive target) on 1..3 points; Lean proves the general statements.
